content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a method that splits a dataset into N parts and trains one neural network on each part. The joint data/model parallel method is amiable for GPU implementation. The proposed method is evaluated on both ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-21K dataset with various architectures like AlexNet-spectral, VGG-16-spectral, ResNet-34-spectral, CycleMLP-spectral and MobileVit-spectral
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strength
* The proposed method and workflow are clear and easy to follow. 
* The motivation of ensemble learning seems to make sense for some applications and scenarios. 
* The proposed method is evaluated on large-scale datasets (e.g., ImageNet1K and ImageNet21K) and demonstrates improvement over conventional classification neural networks. 


### Weaknesses
* Motivation for the proposed dataset splitting is unclear. For example, why does one want to split the dataset in the spectral domain? How about other domains (e.g., labels)?  In addition, why does one want to do the DCT in the final dimension? 
* The advantage of bagging is the parallelism of training. Moreover, it may be interesting to show the results of boosting as another type of ensemble. 
* On ImageNet-21K, the drop in accuracy cannot be ignored. However, the reduction of training time seems limited. 
* What is the fundamental improvement of this method against the well-known bagging or boosting theory? 
* Missing reference on the ensemble of neural networks [1].

 [1] Zhu, Shilin, Xin Dong, and Hao Su. "Binary ensemble neural network: More bits per network or more networks per bit?." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2019.
content.summary_of_the_review: As mentioned before, I have concerns about the novelty of the proposed method (against well-known bagging and boosting theories) and the limited results (in terms of speedup and degradation of accuracy).

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new ensemble learning approach that first transforms the input data set into a Q spectral subsets. An ensemble network is trained for every spectral subset. During inference, the data item is similarly decomposed into its spectral subset that are passed through the trained ensembles. The authors show how to map this training process to GPUs and evaluate it on standard image processing data sets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
-= S1 =- The idea of using spectral decomposition before ensemble training is interesting, and it reduces memory and compute time. In particular, this allows for training with larger models and data using less memory. 

-= S2 =- The idea is simple and elegant and can be easily implemented in any modern deep learning framework. 

-= W1 =- The paper can benefit from spelling out how this space and compute intensity reduction happens. Right now, the paper does not explain that adequately. 

-= W2 =- The terms used in the paper can be captured in the form of a table, it will make it easy to follow the paper. 

-= W3 =- Similarly, the baseline are not clearly explained. What is tNN? How does this work connects with other training optimization approaches such as TreeNets and MotherNets? 

-= W4 =- The experimental section can benefit from some depth. What is the breakdown in the training time between spectral decomposition and training? Where does the memory saving come from? What is the effect of Q? etc. 

-= W5 =- Several typset errors, please revise thoroughly.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity and quality is okay, novelty is reasonable.
content.summary_of_the_review: The idea is nice and simple but not sufficiently explained and analyzed. All that makes assessment hard.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes to apply ensemble learning for training various models on sub-dataset in the spectral domain.
The dataset is split into multiple orthogonal spectral sets; Then the neural network is split into parallel, that are trained independently on the corresponding spectral sets; Finally, the outputs are ensembled to yield final output. With this the paper achieves compression and speedup in training time.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper weaknesses are:
The paper evaluated their methods on alexnet, vgg which are outdated models and trained on toy datasets (mnist, cifar10). The authors should test on more updated models such as: ViT, transformers

The achieved speedup and compression from the proposed method comes at cost of accuracy drop.

The paper should present results with comparison to previous literature methods

The paper should also add inference time of the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is hard to read and understand, several spelling mistakes and broken reference links.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This is a poorly written paper and hard to understand. 
The paper fails to show relevant data to support the proposed method of combining spectral domain CNNs with model ensemble.
And proper comparison with other literature methods isn't well presented.

content.title: Highly Parallel Deep Ensemble Learning
content.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel highly parallel deep ensemble learning, which leads to highly compact and  parallel deep neural networks. The main idea is to \textit{split data into spectral subsets; train subnetworks separately; and ensemble the output results in the inference stage}. The proposed method has parallel branches with each branch being an independent neural network trained using one spectral subset of the training data. It ensembles the outputs of the parallel branches to produce an overall network with substantially stronger generalization capability. It can also scale up the model to the large scale dataset with limited memory. The joint data/model parallel method is amiable for GPU implementation.  Due to the reduced size of inputs,  the proposed spectral tensor network exhibits an inherent network compression, which leads to the acceleration of training process.  We evaluate the proposed spectral tensor networks on the MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet data sets, to highlight that they simultaneously achieve network compression, reduction in computation and parallel speedup. Specifically, on both ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-21K dataset, our proposed AlexNet-spectral, VGG-16-spectral, ResNet-34-spectral, CycleMLP-spectral and MobileVit-spectral networks achieve a comparable performance with the vanila ones, and enjoy up to $4 \times$ compression ratio and $1.5 \times$ speedups.
